the lithium problem is not solved yet.
the Cameron–Fowell mechanism is the only one able to explain the observed Li abundance in the Galaxy.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

lithium production by novae is not as efficient as previously thought, while the production by AGB stars is much more important than generally assumed, and may explain the observed Li abundance of the Galaxy, and the low abundances observed in some Galactic globular clusters.
lithium is produced in the Galaxy in a number of different sites, with different efficiencies, and with a different time–scales for its release.
the Cameron–Fowell process is a very efficient way of producing lithium, and it is very likely that the bulk of the galactic lithium comes from novae and AAG stars.
